2-1.title: Hunter-Gatherers and Human Migration
2-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — HUNTER-GATHERERS AND EARLY MIGRATION

For most of human history, people were hunter-gatherers. This means they hunted wild animals for meat and gathered wild plants, nuts, fruits, and roots for food. Because the food was wild and ran out in each area, hunter-gatherers were nomads — they moved from place to place following animal herds and ripe plants instead of building permanent towns.

Archaeologists, scientists who study the things ancient people left behind, find the oldest evidence of humans in AFRICA. From there, people slowly spread, or migrated, across the whole planet. Scientists trace these journeys by following clues like bones, stone tools, and cave art left along the way.

These long migrations carried people and their cultures to nearly every continent. As small groups moved into new lands, they adapted to different climates, learned new skills, and spread human culture around the world. Movement, not staying still, was the normal way of life for early humans.

questions.question: For MOST of human history, people lived as

questions.question: Which continent is considered the starting point of human migration?

2-2.title: The Agricultural Revolution
2-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE AGRICULTURAL REVOLUTION

About 10,000 years ago, some groups of people learned to plant crops and raise animals. This huge change is called the Agricultural Revolution (also called the Neolithic Revolution). Instead of always moving to find food, farmers could stay in one place. People who settle in one place are leading a sedentary life.

Farming had powerful effects. People could grow and store EXTRA food, called a surplus. With a food surplus, not everyone had to farm. Some people could become builders, priests, traders, soldiers, or leaders instead. This is called a division of labor, or specialization of jobs.

Staying in one place also let people build permanent homes and grow into larger communities, which slowly became villages, towns, and eventually cities. The Agricultural Revolution was a turning point: it changed humans from wandering hunter-gatherers into settled farmers and set the stage for the first civilizations.

questions.question: Which word describes a settled, stay-in-one-place way of living?
questions.explanation: A settled, stay-in-one-place life is called sedentary.

questions.question: Besides planting crops, what else did people learn to do during the Agricultural Revolution?
questions.explanation: During the Agricultural Revolution people learned to plant crops and raise animals.

questions.question: A farmer grows more grain than her family can eat and stores the extra. What is the stored extra called?

questions.question: Which would you expect to find in a settled farming community but NOT in a nomadic hunter-gatherer band?

questions.question: Which is NOT a job that became possible because of a food surplus?

questions.question: What is the MAIN reason the Agricultural Revolution is so important in history?

questions.explanation: It turned wandering hunters into settled farmers and set the stage for the first civilizations.

questions.question: Which word means 'extra'?

questions.question: Before the Agricultural Revolution, almost everyone had to spend their time

2-3.title: The Characteristics of a Civilization
2-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS — WHAT MAKES A CIVILIZATION

A civilization is more than just a big group of people. Historians look for several key features, or characteristics, to call a society a civilization. These usually include: (1) cities, (2) an organized government, (3) a writing system, (4) specialized jobs, (5) social classes (groups ranked high to low), and (6) a shared religion or culture. Often advanced technology, art, and public buildings are added too.

Learning to work metals helped these societies grow. During the Bronze Age, people mixed copper and tin to make bronze, a strong metal used for better tools and weapons. Stronger tools improved farming and building, and stronger weapons helped armies.

Spotting these characteristics helps us tell a true civilization apart from a small village. A small farming village might have homes and fields, but if it lacks cities, writing, government, and specialized jobs, it has not yet become a full civilization. These shared features appear again and again in the great early civilizations you will study.

questions.explanation: Cities and organized government are core features of a civilization.

questions.question: How did learning to make bronze tools and weapons help early societies?

questions.explanation: Bronze gave stronger tools and weapons, helping societies grow.

questions.question: Having builders, priests, and traders instead of everyone farming shows which feature?
questions.explanation: Different specialized jobs are a characteristic of civilization.

questions.question: What helps historians tell a true civilization apart from a small village?

choices.B: The presence of features like cities, writing, and government
choices.D: Whether it is hot or cold there

questions.explanation: Key features such as cities, writing, and government mark a civilization.

questions.question: A small farming village has homes and fields but no cities, writing, or government. It is BEST described as what?
questions.explanation: Without the key characteristics, a village is not yet a full civilization.

questions.question: A shared religion or culture is one characteristic of a civilization. What does 'shared' mean here?

choices.A: Each person believes something totally different
choices.B: Many people in the society hold common beliefs or customs

questions.explanation: A shared culture or religion means common beliefs and customs across the people.

questions.question: Which list correctly names THREE characteristics of a civilization?
questions.explanation: Cities, writing, and organized government are all civilization characteristics.

questions.question: During the Bronze Age, what two metals were mixed to make bronze?
questions.explanation: Bronze is made by mixing copper and tin.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the key characteristics of a civilization?
questions.explanation: Having no leaders or government is not a characteristic; civilizations have an organized government.

questions.question: Why is a writing system so useful to a civilization?

choices.C: It replaces the need for food
choices.D: It lets people record laws, trade, and ideas

questions.explanation: A writing system lets people record laws, trade, and ideas, which helps a civilization run.

questions.question: A society has homes and fields but no cities, no writing, and no government. It is BEST called a

choices.C: small village, not yet a full civilization

questions.explanation: Without cities, writing, and government, it is a small village, not yet a full civilization.

questions.question: What does it mean for a society to have 'social classes'?

choices.A: Groups of people are ranked from higher to lower

questions.explanation: Social classes means groups of people are ranked from higher to lower in a society.

questions.question: How did stronger bronze tools help farming?

choices.A: They made it harder to grow food
choices.C: They let farmers work the land more easily and effectively
choices.D: They were used only for art

questions.explanation: Stronger bronze tools let farmers work the land more easily, improving farming.

questions.question: Which is an example of a 'public building' that might be found in a civilization?

choices.B: A large temple where many people worship

questions.explanation: A large temple where many people worship is an example of a public building in a civilization.

questions.question: An organized government in a civilization MAINLY helps to

choices.C: make rules and keep order for many people

questions.explanation: An organized government makes rules and keeps order for the many people in a civilization.

questions.question: Why is bronze better than copper alone for making weapons?

choices.D: Bronze is stronger than copper alone

questions.explanation: Mixing copper with tin makes bronze, which is stronger than copper alone, so it makes better weapons.

questions.question: Which group of words all name characteristics of a civilization?
questions.explanation: Cities, writing, government, and social classes are all characteristics of a civilization.

questions.question: A 'shared religion or culture' means that many people in the society

choices.D: hold common beliefs, customs, or traditions

questions.explanation: A shared religion or culture means many people hold common beliefs, customs, or traditions.

questions.question: Which best shows 'specialized jobs' in a civilization?

choices.A: A scribe writes, a soldier fights, and a potter makes pots
choices.B: Everyone in the city farms only

questions.explanation: Specialized jobs means different people do different work, like a scribe, a soldier, and a potter.

questions.question: The Bronze Age is named after

choices.B: a metal people learned to make and use

questions.explanation: The Bronze Age is named for bronze, a metal people learned to make and use for tools and weapons.

questions.question: Which question would a historian ask to decide if a society is a civilization?

choices.B: How many clouds are in the sky?
choices.C: Does it have cities, writing, and government?

questions.explanation: A historian checks for key features like cities, writing, and government to identify a civilization.

questions.question: How did better bronze weapons affect armies?

choices.A: They helped armies become stronger in battle
choices.D: They were never used in fighting

questions.explanation: Stronger bronze weapons helped armies become more powerful in battle.

questions.question: Which is the BEST definition of a civilization?

choices.A: Any group of two or three people
choices.B: A complex society with cities, government, writing, and specialized jobs
choices.C: A single farm with one family
choices.D: A group that moves constantly with no homes

questions.explanation: A civilization is a complex society with cities, government, writing, and specialized jobs.

questions.question: A village develops a king, builds a city, and invents writing. It is changing into a
questions.explanation: Gaining a government, a city, and writing means a village is becoming a civilization.

questions.question: Which is NOT a metal involved in making bronze?

choices.C: The mix of copper and tin

questions.explanation: Bronze is made from copper and tin; gold is not used to make bronze.

questions.question: Why do the same characteristics appear in many different early civilizations?

choices.B: They all spoke the same language
choices.C: It happened only by accident once
choices.D: These shared features are what allow complex societies to grow and work

questions.explanation: The same characteristics appear repeatedly because these shared features let complex societies grow and function.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a characteristic with an example?

choices.A: Social classes — everyone is exactly equal
choices.B: Writing system — a clay tablet with symbols

questions.explanation: A clay tablet with symbols is an example of a writing system, one characteristic of civilization.

questions.question: Compared with a small village, a civilization usually has

choices.B: cities, writing, and an organized government

questions.explanation: Unlike a small village, a civilization usually has cities, writing, and an organized government.

questions.question: Advanced technology, art, and public buildings are often signs of a
questions.explanation: Advanced technology, art, and public buildings are often added signs of a civilization.

questions.question: Which sentence shows the correct cause and effect about bronze?

questions.explanation: Learning to make bronze (cause) gave people stronger tools and weapons (effect).

questions.question: Which is the BEST title for a list that includes cities, government, writing, and social classes?
questions.explanation: Cities, government, writing, and social classes are all characteristics of a civilization.

questions.question: In a society with social classes, which statement is TRUE?

questions.explanation: In a society with social classes, some groups have higher rank or status than others.

questions.question: Why might a civilization need a writing system MORE than a small wandering band does?

choices.D: Small bands trade far more than cities

questions.question: Which of these is an organized government MOST likely to do?

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of 'specialized jobs' that a food surplus made possible in a civilization?

questions.explanation: Priests, soldiers, and traders who do not farm are specialized jobs made possible by a food surplus.

questions.question: Which statement about the Bronze Age is TRUE?

choices.A: People used only stone and never metal
choices.C: People learned to make bronze for better tools and weapons

questions.explanation: During the Bronze Age, people learned to make bronze, which gave them better tools and weapons.

questions.question: What is the MOST important big idea of this lesson?

choices.B: Bronze was useless to early people
choices.C: Writing is the only thing that matters
choices.D: Civilizations share key features like cities, writing, government, and specialized jobs

questions.explanation: The big idea is that civilizations share key features such as cities, writing, government, and specialized jobs.
